title: Canotto Lab full backup
description: Everything at once: the recipe library, the bake log and the baker's settings. A restore replaces the lot.

settings.description: Preferences and the fermentation model. Only part of this travels between devices. settings.model, the Q10 constants every figure is computed from, is shared: two devices holding different constants would produce different plans from the same recipe, so the later word wins, ranked by settings.modelUpdatedAt. The display unit and the other preferences stay on the device that set them, because whether a phone shows Celsius is that phone's business.

unit.description: Display only. Stored temperatures are always Celsius.

refTempC.description: One fermentation unit is one hour at this temperature.

q10Warm.description: Rate multiplier per 10 degrees, at and above the cold break.

q10Cold.description: Steeper multiplier below it, because a fridge slows dough more than one Q10 predicts.

q10Enzyme.description: Rate multiplier per 10 degrees for the flour's own enzymes, which slow far less in the cold than yeast does. Maturation units are integrated against this curve, and a flour's W value bounds how many of them its gluten can absorb.

optimumC.description: Temperature above which yeast activity falls away again.

modelUpdatedAt.description: When the fermentation model was last changed, used to rank the two sides when syncing. Absent on a model nobody has touched, which loses to one that has been.

current.title: The bake in progress
current.description: The session as it stands: which recipe is loaded, the schedule being followed, which protocol steps are ticked and when each was really done, plus any measurements and scores recorded so far. This is one working session rather than a collection, so it cannot be merged item by item: half of one schedule joined to half of another is a bake nobody ran. One side wins whole. A session with work in it beats one without, where work means any ticked step, recorded time, measurement, score or note; only when both have work, or neither does, does it come down to the later updatedAt. Ranking by time alone is not enough, because a device that was merely opened and poked at carries a later stamp while carrying no bake. A session nobody has touched has no updatedAt and loses to anything.

id.description: The session's own id, which the bake record keeps when it is filed. Photographs are attached by it, so they are on the bake from the moment they are taken. A session loaded from storage keeps the id it was saved with; only one that has never had an id is given a new one.

leadHours.description: How many hours from the first mix to the launch, as chosen on the recipe that was loaded. Null when the session follows the schedule's own arithmetic rather than a figure set on the recipe.

equipment.description: The mixer and oven this session is being run on. Equipment belongs to the baker rather than to the recipe, so it travels with the session and is copied onto the bake record when one is filed.

done.description: Ids of the protocol steps ticked off.

doneAt.description: When each step was actually ticked, as milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Same shape and meaning as on a bake, including that it never runs backwards: a step is never recorded earlier than the last step ticked before it.

actuals.description: What has been measured so far, in the same shape a filed bake carries. A session is a bake that has not been filed yet, so the two hold measurements identically.

scores.description: The marks given so far, in the same shape a filed bake carries. Present and unscored until the run is judged at the end.

notes.description: Whatever the baker has written about this run so far. Carried onto the bake record when it is filed.

updatedAt.description: When the session was last edited. Absent or null on a session nobody has touched, which always loses to one that has.

photos.title: Photographs
photos.description: What pictures exist and which bake each belongs to. Descriptions only: the pictures themselves are separate files stored alongside this one and named photo-<id>.jpg, so this document stays small enough to sync in a moment however many photographs there are. A picture never changes once taken, so these merge as a union by id rather than by which copy is newer, and a file already present never needs sending again.

bakeId.description: The bake this belongs to, filed or still in progress. A session carries the id it will be filed under, so a picture taken at the bench is on the right bake before the record exists and is never re-attached. If a sync replaces this device's session with another device's, pictures pointing at the session that lost are moved to the one that survived, since both are the same bake and a picture attached to nothing is reachable from no screen.

bytes.description: Size after scaling down, not the size of the original.

photosRemoved.title: Photographs deliberately deleted
photosRemoved.description: Ids of pictures that have been deleted. Because the descriptions above merge as a union, a deletion with no record of itself would simply be undone by the other device on the next sync, bytes and all. Anything listed here is removed from that union and its file deleted from storage. This is the one place the app's usual rule, that a sync never deletes anything, is deliberately set aside: a picture removed on purpose is expensive to carry and obvious when it returns.

bakesRemoved.title: Bakes deliberately deleted
bakesRemoved.description: Ids of bakes that have been deleted on purpose. A merge keeps both sides, which is right for an edit made in two places and wrong for a deletion: with no record of it the other device simply returns what was thrown away. Anything listed here is removed from the merge on both sides and stays removed. Deleting a bake also deletes its photographs, so without this a deleted bake came back without its pictures, which is neither the record nor its absence.

recipesRemoved.title: Recipes deliberately deleted
recipesRemoved.description: Ids of recipes that have been deleted on purpose, applied to the merge the same way as bakesRemoved. Bakes logged against a deleted recipe are kept: a bake carries its own copy of the dough and protocol, so it stays readable, and its recipeId may point at a recipe that no longer exists.
